_readme: Reviewed (unit, code) pairs for Quantities emitted against the UCUM system.
Key format is "<unit>|<code>", where unit is the human-readable Quantity.unit
and code is the machine-readable Quantity.code.
The rule, decided 2026-07-26: Quantity.unit carries UCUM's OWN name for the code.
check-units.mjs verifies that against @lhncbc/ucum-lhc, so a correct pair needs no
entry here at all — the gate looks the name up rather than trusting a signature.
That is why this file is short and does not grow with the codebase.
status 'rejected'  -> the pair is wrong. Fatal, with the recorded reason. These are
kept after the defect is fixed, as regression guards.
status 'exception' -> UCUM publishes no usable name for this code, so the rule
cannot be applied. Must say why. Per-code and narrow.
status 'approved'  -> historical note on a pair that now passes the name check on
its own. Kept for the record, not consulted by the gate.
A unit gate compares a label to a code. It cannot see that the VALUE is in a
different scale — 1.48 deg is structurally perfect whether or not the source sent
radians. Pairs whose real risk is a data defect carry a 'guarded_by' note naming
the numeric tests that protect them. Deleting those tests removes the protection.
"unitless" records Quantities that carry a value and deliberately no unit, keyed
by file. A missing unit is normally a defect, so an entry here needs a reason and
an occurrence count. The count is the guard: it is checked exactly, so adding a
new bare Quantity to a waived file fails the gate rather than inheriting the
sign-off written for a different one. Keying by line was rejected — a line number
drifts under any edit above it and the waiver would quietly move to another
Quantity. A waiver that matches nothing is stale and also fails.

steps|steps.reason: 'steps' is not a UCUM code. UCUM expresses countable things as annotations.
steps|steps.suggested: unit 'steps', code '{steps}'. The same file already uses {score} and {count} correctly.

MET-min|min.reason: MET-minutes is not minutes. A receiver reading code 'min' interprets 300 MET-minutes as 300 minutes of activity.
MET-min|min.suggested: There is no UCUM code for MET-min. Use an annotation such as '{MET-min}', or emit the value under a vendor-local system.

degree|deg.reason: UCUM publishes the name of 'deg' as "degree - plane angle". That trailing phrase disambiguates it from degrees of temperature in UCUM's own tables; it is not part of the unit's name, and putting it in Quantity.unit would read as a unit nobody uses. 'degree' is the name with the disambiguator removed.
degree|deg.guarded_by: A unit gate cannot detect a value in the wrong scale — 1.48 deg is structurally perfect. The guard is numeric: provider-vitronic asserts a known angle reads ~84.89 degrees, and fhir-core asserts 1 rad converts to 57.2957795 deg via @lhncbc/ucum-lhc. This pair was 'rejected' until that conversion existed; what it flagged was a DATA defect, not a unit defect. If those tests are deleted, this pair loses its protection.
degree|deg.reviewed: Martin Etzrodt, PhD, Open Science Foundation, 2026-07-26

\u00b0C|Cel.reason: Used for a temperature deviation, not an absolute temperature. UCUM 'Cel' denotes a point on the Celsius scale; a difference is 'K'.

meter|m.reason: 'meter' is UCUM's own name for 'm', so this now passes the name check unaided. The entry is kept as a record: it was 'rejected' because provider-vitronic applied it to cross-section AREA values, which were also emitted as 'm2' at the top level of the same resource — the same number appearing once as an area and once as a length. That was a DATA defect, not a unit defect, and a unit gate cannot express "correct for a length, wrong for an area".
meter|m.guarded_by: provider-vitronic now applies METRE only to circumference and distanceFromRoot, and SQUARE_METRE to areas. The guard is in the tests that pin areas to 'm2': crosssection.unit.test.ts and bundleBuilder.integration.test.ts.
meter|m.reviewed: Martin Etzrodt, PhD, Open Science Foundation, 2026-07-26

%|%.reason: UCUM defines '%' as a real unit atom (Table 3, = 10*-2) but publishes no name for it, so the name rule has nothing to check against. '%' is its own readable form. The consequence that matters is the scale: because '%' is a true atom rather than an annotation, 95% is sent as 95 and never as 0.95. Do not write '{percent}'.
%|%.reviewed: Martin Etzrodt, PhD, Open Science Foundation, 2026-07-26

1|1.reason: The UCUM unity. UCUM names it '1', which is the code itself, so the name rule is vacuous here. Used only where the quantity is genuinely dimensionless: heartbeat entropy, VO2max covariance, surface-normal vector components, and allelic frequency under LOINC 81258-6, whose property is NFr — a number fraction in [0,1], never a percentage. Bare '1' was chosen over an annotation because these are dimensionless in fact, not merely unlabelled.
1|1.reviewed: Martin Etzrodt, PhD, Open Science Foundation, 2026-07-26

US ring size|{ring_size}.reason: UCUM annotations cannot contain a space — '{US ring size}' is rejected by the grammar — so the code has to stay the machine token '{ring_size}', whose stripped name is 'ring_size'. The readable form names the sizing scale, and a ring size without it is not interpretable: US 8 and EU 57 are the same ring. The annotation carries no meaning to a receiver either way, since a conformant parser discards it and reads the unity.
US ring size|{ring_size}.reviewed: Martin Etzrodt, PhD, Open Science Foundation, 2026-07-26

packages/provider-vitronic/src/fhir/mapp.reason: VITRONIC BodyLoop scan properties are untyped key/value pairs and the API states no unit for them anywhere in the payload. The mapper emits the number with no unit rather than asserting a UCUM unit nobody has verified, which ground rule 1 forbids and which would be the worse error: a wrong unit is silently interpretable, a missing one is visibly incomplete. FHIR permits a Quantity with only a value, and the HL7 validator reports no error on the emitted bundle.
packages/provider-vitronic/src/fhir/mapp.resolved_by: A reviewed property_path -> unit table, tracked as TODO(clinical-review) in the mapper. Once it exists the paths with a known unit carry one and this waiver shrinks or goes away.
packages/provider-vitronic/src/fhir/mapp.reviewed: Martin Etzrodt, PhD, Open Science Foundation, 2026-07-26
